articles.headline: AWS adds native CloudFormation drift detection – what builders need to know
articles.dek: A new built‑in drift‑scan lets you compare live resources to the stored template and generate an up‑to‑date CloudFormation file, closing the gap between console clicks and IaC.

body.text: Key Takeaway

AWS now offers a built‑in drift‑scan for CloudFormation stacks that compares live resources to the stored definition and can emit an updated template reflecting the current state [FACT:ea247c3fb7569e75574fbf9070e67368][FACT:25d698d53e9bc10f688c2a56b076c47b]. Builders get a shortcut to pull accidental console edits back under version control.
Why This Matters

AWS accounts often grow organically, with teams making manual edits through the Management Console over time [FACT:80434c29cb30e942989248f74cc7a06c][FACT:b34160d270e1c6c3bedefe0dc5a1ecaf][FACT:5f2eb0441a206254b3a163dfe2811fcf]. Those ad‑hoc changes create drift that makes stacks unpredictable and forces “click‑ops” instead of Git‑ops [FACT:84f3434d8510b540aed956f4e6015131][FACT:38f7ee6d5adf2aa6c08053294bc0cfb3].
What Happened

The AWS DevOps Blog announced on Aug 21 2026 that the drift‑scan is generally available and is powered by the same IaC generator that produces CloudFormation templates [FACT:633562543207720b749a64c0c792eb39][FACT:ea247c3fb7569e75574fbf9070e67368].
Builder View

If you run Kubernetes on AWS, add the drift‑scan as a cheap validation step in your staging pipeline. Run the scan, review the generated template, and commit any differences – this keeps your IaC catalog aligned with reality and avoids technical debt from ad‑hoc console changes [FACT:ea247c3fb7569e75574fbf9070e67368][FACT:25d698d53e9bc10f688c2a56b076c47b].
Ardur Take

The announcement is a single‑source AWS release, but the feature is production‑ready and matches best practices for IaC governance. Early adoption of the scan helps keep drift under control [FACT:ea247c3fb7569e75574fbf9070e67368].

keyPoints: Native drift‑scan detects live‑resource vs. template mismatches and can generate a fresh CloudFormation file [FACT:ea247c3fb7569e75574fbf9070e67368][FACT:25d698d53e9bc10f688c2a56b076c47b].
Manual console edits accumulate over time, creating hidden drift that the new tool surfaces [FACT:80434c29cb30e942989248f74cc7a06c][FACT:5f2eb0441a206254b3a163dfe2811fcf].
The feature is built into the same IaC generator that AWS already uses for template creation [FACT:633562543207720b749a64c0c792eb39].
articles.whyItMatters: Drift makes infrastructure unpredictable and forces teams to “click around” instead of using version‑controlled IaC; the new scan gives builders a way to keep CloudFormation stacks honest.
articles.readerAction: Run `aws cloudformation detect-drift --stack-name <your-stack>` in a staging environment, inspect the generated template, and commit any changes to your Git repository.

references.title: From clickops to governed IaC: CloudFormation drift detection in practice
